records.classification: New original trial; comparator context for this profile
records.design: Phase 2b randomized study in biopsy-confirmed MASH with F2–F3 fibrosis. 386 randomized; 381 treated. Three blinded efinopegdutide arms and placebo; separate open-label semaglutide reference arm. 52-week histological endpoints. Merck funded.
records.findings: Efinopegdutide improved MASH resolution versus placebo. Fibrosis improvement varied by dose; the highest dose did not achieve statistical significance on that endpoint. Gastrointestinal events and discontinuations matter. Semaglutide was a reference treatment, not the principal investigational agent.
records.limits: Abstract-only review. Reported primary-endpoint denominators differ from treated-arm sizes despite a stated missing-biopsy-as-failure analysis; resolve analysis populations in full text before reusing numerical estimates. Do not transfer efinopegdutide benefits or harms to semaglutide, infer superiority over the reference arm, or infer regulatory authorization.
records.reason: Existing semaglutide profile makes no claim from this trial and contains no misattribution to correct. A comparator-context study is not automatically irrelevant, but no numerical or efficacy addition is warranted from the currently accessible material.

records.classification: New exploratory follow-up of an overlapping trial population
records.design: TOGETHER-PsA, NCT06588296: phase 3b randomized open-label assessor-blinded trial, 271 adults, ixekizumab plus tirzepatide (138) versus ixekizumab alone (133). Earlier week-36 results and current week-52 outcomes are the same trial, not independent replications. Lilly sponsored.
records.findings: At 52 weeks ACR50 was 43.7% versus 15.7%; abstract reports no new safety concerns. Add a narrowly framed follow-up summary with trial identity, treatment arms and population.
records.limits: Week-52 endpoints are prespecified but exploratory and not multiplicity-controlled. Open-label treatment can affect reported outcomes despite assessor blinding. No tirzepatide-only arm; no monotherapy efficacy inference for PsA. Abstract-only review cannot fully assess missing data, detailed adverse-event rates or all author conflicts. Sample and duration cannot rule out rare harms. This review makes no new approval claim.
records.reason: The profile did not previously cover TOGETHER-PsA; longer follow-up adds relevant combination context while preserving uncertainty. New source added to correction monitoring and only this profile appraisal date advanced.

records.classification: Contextual simulated-patient research; not a new medication adverse-event signal
records.design: Cross-sectional covert simulated-patient encounters at 384 urban pharmacies in three Jordanian governorates. Scripted scenarios include suspected semaglutide-associated pancreatitis, empagliflozin-associated ketoacidosis and apixaban-associated bleeding.
records.findings: Measures recognition, triage and reporting behavior, not adverse events in medication-exposed patients.
records.limits: Scripted encounters and selected urban settings limit generalizability. Cannot estimate pancreatitis incidence, establish medication causality, or demonstrate a new safety risk.
records.reason: No current profile statement relies on this study. No medication-safety wording change warranted. Future title-identified simulated/standardized-patient studies receive a contextual-study alert rather than safety-signal; the alert remains queued for review.

regulatory_review: No regulatory updates inferred from these publications. Official regulatory review remains separate under the monitor README.
